memos.headline: Defensive Rotation Intact: XOM and UNH Lead While Mega-Cap Tech Breaks Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of March 28. The mega-cap tech names—NVDA (-26.6% from highs, RSI 39), GOOGL (-25.2%, RSI 32.8), AMZN (-20.4%, RSI 37.3)—are in confirmed downtrends, trading well below both their 50-day and 200-day averages with deteriorating relative strength versus SPY. On the other side, XOM stands out as the strongest chart in the group: +11.3% over 12 weeks, 6.2% above its 50-day, RSI 66 (strong but not overbought), and a remarkable +16.9% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks. UNH and PG are also showing clear defensive leadership with positive 4-week and 12-week relative strength, low ATR, and prices hugging their moving averages. I have no conviction that the tech selloff is done—GOOGL's RSI at 32.8 could produce a bounce, but the trend is firmly lower and I'd need to see closes back above the 50-day averages before turning constructive.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: above both moving averages, +16.9% 12w relative strength vs SPY, low volatility; would reassess on a close below $111 (200d area).
Positive 4w relative strength of +15.1% vs SPY with RSI 58.8 and low ATR of 1.82%; above 50d mean, would exit below $490.
Flat to its 50d and 200d means with only -6.5% drawdown and positive relative strength—classic defensive hold; invalidated below $160.
RSI 32.8 is the lowest in the group, -14.2% below 50d mean, -25.2% from highs with -13.8% 12w relative weakness; no reason to step in until a close above $170.
Down 26.6% from highs with 4.56% ATR making it the most volatile name here; 12w relative strength -14.7% vs SPY screams broken trend; need a reclaim of $125 (50d area) to reconsider.
RSI 37.3, -11.1% below 50d mean, and -20.4% drawdown with negative relative strength on all timeframes; would need a close above $210 to turn neutral.
Down 19% from highs and below both averages, but 4w relative strength vs SPY is slightly positive at +1.9%, suggesting it may be stabilizing; watching $395 as the level to clear.
Still above 200d mean (+5.6%) with strong 26w return of +15.4%, but the 4w -8.2% pullback and -5.6% gap below 50d suggest a pause; support at $230 is key.
Below both moving averages with -8.1% 12w relative weakness vs SPY; trend is down but less extreme than GOOGL/NVDA; would turn neutral above $230.
RSI 38.1, -20.9% from highs, below both averages by 7-9%; cyclical weakness confirmed by price; need a close above $355 to reconsider.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Strongest Earnings Power; XOM and UNH Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin, only $8.46B debt) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin, $14.79B debt), both combining top-line growth with expanding profitability and conservative balance sheets. MSFT at 34.6% net margin and 12.3% revenue growth remains a compounding machine, though I want to see Azure segment margins hold before raising conviction further. On the other side, XOM's revenue declined 1.1% YoY with a thin 9.1% net margin, and UNH posted only 1.6% net income growth on 5.5% margins with $76.90B in debt—both signal cash-flow compression risk that I'm unwilling to pay for. CAT's 5.0% revenue decline concerns me despite margin resilience at 17.2%; I need to see order book stabilization before turning constructive.

views.note: Extraordinary 56.2% net margin and 77.9% revenue growth on minimal leverage ($8.46B debt) represent best-in-class earnings power; would reassess if gross margins compress below 60%.
Revenue +11.8% YoY with 27.5% net margin and only $14.79B debt offers a compelling growth-at-reasonable-leverage profile; net income +28.3% shows operating leverage kicking in.
34.6% net margin is the highest among mega-cap software peers and 12.3% revenue growth is durable; total debt of $44.97B is manageable but I want cloud segment detail to raise conviction.
Net income nearly doubled YoY (+88.3%) as margin expanded to 10.7%, but $58B debt and still-thin margins mean I need to see AWS profitability sustain before going higher conviction.
Solid 29.2% net margin but only 4% revenue growth and $94.80B in total debt suggest limited upside from here without a new product cycle re-accelerating the top line.
Net income surged 50.5% YoY to $14.01B with a 32.7% margin, but the $401B debt stack and cyclical credit risk keep me from going outright long; would turn positive on sustained NII trends.
Net income +33.5% YoY looks impressive but revenue grew only 2.1%, suggesting margin gains may be one-time; 21.2% net margin is healthy but top-line stagnation limits upside.
Revenue -1.1% and net income -0.3% YoY with a 9.1% net margin signal commodity-driven earnings compression; would reconsider only if upstream volumes or pricing materially improve.
Only 1.6% net income growth on a 5.5% net margin with $76.90B in debt is the weakest earnings-power profile in this universe; medical cost ratio trends would need to reverse for me to engage.
Revenue declined 5.0% YoY and while 17.2% net margin held up, $31.74B in debt against a shrinking top line raises cycle-risk concerns; order backlog stabilization would change my view.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Sticky Inflation—Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, even as the trailing 12-month CPI print sits at 2.8% and the 3-month annualized pace (~4%) suggests inflation is re-accelerating. Unemployment at 4.2% is stable over three months but up 30bp year-over-year, signaling a slow-motion softening rather than outright deterioration. The 10y yield at 4.27% has dropped 35bp over three months while the 10y-2y spread has steepened to +41bp, consistent with the market pricing eventual easing but not imminently. In this pause-with-sticky-inflation regime, I favor sectors that benefit from elevated nominal rates (banks) and defensive cash-flow compounders (staples, healthcare), while I am cautious on high-duration growth names whose valuations are most sensitive to a 'higher for longer' path. A March CPI print showing 3-month annualized core above 4% or a sudden jump in unemployment above 4.5% would be the catalysts that change this call.

views.note: Banks benefit from a steep and positive 10y-2y spread (+41bp, up 75bp YoY) and sustained high short rates supporting net interest margins.
Defensive staples with pricing power are well-positioned in a pause regime where inflation remains above target and growth is decelerating.
Healthcare offers defensive cash flows and low duration sensitivity, attractive while the Fed holds rates at 4.50% with no near-term easing signal.
High-duration growth is most vulnerable if the market reprices the 'higher for longer' path; 10y yield still at 4.27% with sticky inflation argues against aggressive multiple expansion.
Quality growth with massive buybacks provides some cushion, but elevated rates and slowing consumer spending keep me from getting constructive.
Recurring revenue base is resilient but valuation is rate-sensitive; pause regime with no imminent cuts keeps me sidelined.
Cyclical bellwether faces cross-currents: stable unemployment supports capex but rising unemployment trend (+30bp YoY) and high rates argue for caution.
Energy is more oil-price driven than rate-driven; macro data alone gives me no strong directional view here.
Consumer-facing cyclicality and high capex intensity make it vulnerable in a higher-for-longer regime, though AWS margins provide offset.
Ad revenue is macro-sensitive and a slowdown in labor markets could weigh, but strong cash generation limits downside; net neutral from macro lens.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Negative Sentiment Washout in NVDA and GOOGL May Be Creating Contrarian Opportunity
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across our universe and looking for names where negative sentiment may have overshot. NVDA dropped 8.5% on its Feb 26 earnings print and GOOGL fell 7.3% on its Feb 4 results—both sharp single-day moves that suggest crowded negative positioning and potential sentiment troughs. AMZN saw a more modest -4.1% reaction on Feb 6, while XOM slipped -2.5% on Jan 31 results. With roughly a month elapsed since these washouts, I have moderate conviction that the worst of the negative narrative has been digested for NVDA and GOOGL, while AAPL and JPM show no earnings-driven sentiment disruption and remain in quieter sentiment regimes.

views.note: The -8.5% post-earnings drop on Feb 27 likely flushed weak hands; subsequent board change on Mar 7 is routine noise, and sentiment should be turning up from a trough.
A -7.3% post-earnings selloff in early Feb was severe; the Mar 18 Reg FD filing suggests management is proactively communicating, which can help stabilize narrative.
The -4.1% earnings reaction was negative but not extreme enough to signal a clear sentiment washout or contrarian entry.
A modest -2.5% post-earnings dip in late January is likely fully absorbed by now with no strong directional sentiment signal remaining.
The Feb 25 shareholder vote filing is procedural with no sentiment catalyst; absence of negative tone is not itself a buy signal.
Bylaws/governance filing in early Feb carries no meaningful sentiment charge; no earnings-driven tone shift to trade around.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Tripled in Three Months—Structural Risk for Tech Supply Chains and Energy
memos.body: I am struck by the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 313, up over 200% in three months, signaling a regime shift in the policy environment that goes well beyond normal quarter-to-quarter noise. High-yield OAS has widened 46 bps in a month to 3.27%, confirming that credit markets are pricing real stress, not just headline risk. VIX at 18.69 has actually pulled back 11.5% over the past month, suggesting equity vol is underpricing the policy tail risk embedded in the uncertainty index. WTI crude at $70.30 is remarkably stable (-1.4% over 3 months), which tells me energy supply disruption is not the primary driver—this is about trade policy, export controls, and potential tariff escalation. I have highest conviction that names with concentrated China/Asia supply chains (AAPL, NVDA) face structural headwinds, while domestically oriented financials and energy names are relatively insulated.

views.note: Export-control escalation risk on advanced AI chips to China remains the dominant structural overhang, and the tripling of policy uncertainty reinforces that this is not a one-quarter event.
Concentrated assembly in China and rising trade-policy uncertainty create a structural supply-chain risk that equity vol is currently underpricing.
WTI stability near $70 and domestic production focus insulate XOM from the trade-policy shock; energy security tailwinds persist.
Widening HY spreads (+46 bps) and a steeper curve (+19 bps in 1m) are mixed—NIM benefits offset by rising credit risk in a high-uncertainty regime.
Less direct supply-chain exposure than hardware peers, but regulatory and antitrust policy risk keeps me from going long amid 313-level uncertainty.
Domestic infrastructure spending is a tailwind, but tariff escalation on steel/materials inputs and global capex slowdown risk roughly offset each other.

Avoid mega-cap tech names where strong fundamentals clash with deteriorating technicals, geopolitical headwinds, and higher-for-longer rate risk.

plans.rationale: Strongest technical trend in the universe (+16.9% 12w relative strength, RSI 66, above both MAs) with geopolitical insulation from trade-policy risk and stable WTI near $70. plans.changes_my_mind: Close below $111 (200-day area) or WTI crude breaking below $65 would invalidate the thesis.
